setting: A fictional practice chat with a language partner about normal weekdays.

presentation.situation: Your language partner {{name}} wants to compare normal weekdays with you. {{name}} {{routine}}. Tell {{name}} about your day and ask about theirs.
presentation.opening: I always find mornings difficult! What does a normal weekday look like for you?

brief.you_are: You are practising English with a partner.
brief.situation: Your language partner {{name}} wants to compare normal weekdays with you. {{name}} {{routine}}. Tell {{name}} about your day and ask about theirs.
brief.task: Say what you usually do on a weekday, use time words like at seven or after work, and ask about your partner's day.
brief.done_looks_like: Your partner knows three things you do in a day and when, and you asked about their day.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are practising English with a partner.
goals: Say what you usually do on a weekday, use time words like at seven or after work, and ask about your partner's day.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Practises English with you each week

card.want: To compare daily routines, and to find a good time for the next practice.
card.hidden_need: Would like to find a regular practice time.
card.speech: Very simple everyday English. Short sentences. One easy question at a time.
tactics: If the answer is very short, ask one easy question
Use the person's own words back to them

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: You meet each week to practise English.

objectives.evidence: The learner describes things they usually do, in the present simple.
alternatives: I usually wake up early and go to work.

objectives.evidence: The learner uses a time expression.

objectives.description: Ask about the other person's routine
objectives.evidence: The learner asks about the partner's routine.
alternatives: What time do you get up?

beats.goal: Hear what the learner usually does.
opportunity: What do you usually do in the morning?
beats.orient: Tell me about a normal day. Start with: I usually.
fallback: What do you usually do in the morning?

opportunity: What time do you do that?
beats.orient: Now say when. You can say: at seven, or: in the evening.
fallback: What time do you do that?

beats.goal: The learner asks about the partner.
opportunity: My day is very different. Do you want to know about it?
Do you have a question about my day?
beats.orient: Now ask about my day. You can say: What time do you get up?
fallback: Do you have a question about my day?
My day is very different. Do you want to know about it?

closing_line: Thanks. That was good practice. See you next week!

o1.good: Using the present simple for things you do every day.
o1.micro_lesson: For daily habits use: I wake up, I go, I eat.
o1.model: I usually wake up early, then I go to work.
o1.smaller_step: Say: I usually, and one action.

o2.good: Time words help the listener follow your day.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: at seven, in the morning, after work.
o2.model: I start work at nine, and in the evening I cook.

o3.good: Asking the same question back is an easy way to keep talking.
o3.micro_lesson: Use: What time do you, or: When do you.
o3.model: What time do you get up? When do you finish work?
o3.smaller_step: Say: What time do you get up?

variants.name: Lina
variants.routine: starts work at eight and goes for a walk after dinner

variants.name: Omar
variants.routine: studies in the morning and works in a shop in the evening
